title: Ignatz Awards Nominate Box Garden Beetle Manga for Outstanding Collection
content:
Glacier Bay Books describes its story:

Unfurling fields of morning glories and buttony polka dots. Wormholes of childhood memories and cabinets of magical curiosities. Balletic bands of laughter and creeping stippled shadows.

Seirinkogeisha published the manga short story collection in Japan in 2004.

Glacier Bay Books first announced its release of the manga in May 2025. It launched a Kickstarter crowdfunding campaign for it along with several other titles in August 2025. The company announced in April that printing was nearly finished, before publishing the collection in English in May.

Ryan Holmberg translated the collection. Tim Sun did the lettering, and Emuh Ruh and Ryan Holmberg were the editors.

The Ignatz Awards, which are named after the character in George Herriman's seminal comic Krazy Kat , recognize "outstanding achievement in comics and cartooning." A jury of cartoonists create a ballot every year, and then the attendees of Small Press Expo vote on the nominees.

The 2024 Ignatz Awards nominated Offshore Lightning , a collection of short manga by author Nazuna Saitō , for "Outstanding Collection."

Glacier Bay Books ' Glaeolia 2 collection of indie manga won the award for the "Outstanding Anthology" category in the 2021 Ignatz Awards.
author: ANN

title: RIDI to Shut Down Japanese Short-Form Live-Action Platform Kanta
content:
Korean content platform RIDI announced on Thursday that it will shut down Kanta, its short-form live-action platform in Japan, as part of a restructuring of its business portfolio.

RIDI launched Kanta in Japan in July 2025, offering short-form dramas based on Korean content. The company said it decided to discontinue the service to focus its resources on its fan community platform business built around comics, webtoons, and web novels amid the rapidly changing global market.

RIDI plans to use the production expertise and user data accumulated through Kanta to expand its intellectual properties and strengthen its related businesses. The company will also explore new ways to utilize the IP assets acquired through the service.

title: Bleach Makes Anime History With Its Latest Episode After Pulling Off Major Changes
content:
Bleach finally returned years after its original run ended to adapt the Thousand-Year Blood War , a story the original anime never depicted. Since summer 2026, the final part of this arc has been airing, and as expected, the series’ final stretch has continued to exceed expectations and blow fans’ minds. In just five episodes, the final stretch of the anime has featured not one but two Bankai that had been concealed for decades , while also introducing a major retcon involving a prominent character. However, there is no doubt that the series’ main character, Ichigo, has been stealing the show in his final confrontation against Yhwach.

However, unlike his battle against Aizen, Ichigo isn’t alone, as Orihime has been following him closely and actively participating in the fight by helping Ichigo heal and shielding him from attacks. The original manga did not feature her role to this extent, making her involvement one of the anime’s notable changes. Meanwhile, the latest episode also features changes to Ichigo’s new Bankai that were not present in the original manga, giving him a new look and expanding its scope. As a result, Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War Episode 45, titled “Defend You,” debuted with a perfect 10/10 score on IMDb, which it maintained until it reached 21,000 ratings, making anime history.

Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War Makes Anime History With a Perfect IMDb Score

Anime episodes debuting with a perfect 10/10 on IMDb are a feat only a few have achieved, with the most recent notable example being an episode from Re:Zero ‘s fourth season, which maintained its 10/10 score with several thousand ratings. However, Bleach has exceeded that achievement with a perfect rating across more than 20,000 ratings. Currently, the episode is rated 9.9 with 27,000 ratings as of this writing. The significance behind Bleach ‘s latest episode achieving such a high rating goes far beyond what the number represents. Tite Kubo, the creator of Bleach , has repeatedly expressed that he wanted to explore even more in the manga’s final moments. However, various constraints forced him to end the series much faster than he intended.

Thus, with the emergence of Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War , Tite Kubo became fully involved in the anime’s production, which led to several major changes. The latest changes involving Orihime have helped address one of the biggest issues in shonen anime: failing to feature compelling female characters. With Orihime’s involvement going to such an extent and her constantly pushing herself, the series has effectively portrayed the notion of love and how it can push individuals to go beyond limits they never imagined.

Meanwhile, without a doubt, the major change was Ichigo’s new Bankai debuting with a completely new look, depicted with Blood Chains, which fans have come to see as a potential tease for the one-shot Hell arc of the franchise. Fans of the series naturally embraced these changes, reflecting that when a creator’s true vision is brought to life, the results can be extraordinary. Bleach having its final arc animated has been one of the biggest wishes of its fans, and seeing it finally come true has fulfilled the fandom, highlighting that when fans get what they want and even more, an anime can make history.

title: Kakao Games Partners With The Grimm Entertainment to Develop Games Based on Webtoons
content:
Kakao Games announced on August 4 that it has agreed to work with webtoon studio The Grimm Entertainment to develop and publish games based on its popular comic and webtoon intellectual properties.

Founded by webtoon artist Taejun Pak , The Grimm Entertainment owns several popular IPs, including Manager Kim , (also known as Agent Kim: Reactivated ) and Lookism , which have gained popularity in both South Korea and international markets. Pak and The Grimm Entertainment are also known for the Viral Hit webtoon, which has inspired both an anime and a Japanese live-action adaptation.

Under the agreement, Kakao Games will adapt The Grimm Entertainment's webtoon IPs into games, expanding its popular titles into new forms of entertainment.

Kakao Games CEO Si-woo Lee said, “We expect our partnership with The Grimm Entertainment, which has powerful IP and a strong fanbase, to bring new experiences to players. We will work closely together to create games that can attract significant interest in global markets.”

The Grimm Entertainment CEO Hyung-soo Ahn said, “We are pleased to work with Kakao Games, which has extensive experience in game services. By combining our IP and webtoons with games, we hope to create another successful example of adapting a single IP across multiple forms of media.”

title: Kingdom Hearts Creator Confirms First Major Details for New Disney+ Anime
content:
Kingdom Hearts is now in the works on an official anime series coming to Disney+, and the creator behind it all has revealed the first details about what to expect from this new entry in a much wider franchise. Kingdom Hearts is preparing for a whole new era of its run with Disney as they are planning to expand its influence out with even more projects. This includes a new anime series, and that’s something that the franchise has been trying to get off the ground for decades at this point but never quite was able to do.

Rumors of a potential Kingdom Hearts anime have been around for a few years , and it was finally confirmed to be in the works as a new anime series was officially announced as part of the D23 event earlier this month. Kingdom Hearts franchise creator Tetsuya Nomura opened up about the new series following its announcement with fans on social media , and confirmed the first few details about this project. It’s going to be telling a brand new story.

What to Know for New Kingdom Hearts Anime

“We can’t discuss all the details just yet, but I’ve been in close discussions with the scenario team, including myself, and when needed, we’ve also enlisted the art team’s cooperation, even creating multiple new character designs specifically for this project,” Nomura revealed in a statement. “I can’t say anything more right now, but the hint is in the single piece of key art that’s been revealed . Please let your imaginations run wild while you await further updates.” But notably this new art is a big tease about what’s next.

Other details confirmed for the new Kingdom Hearts anime is the fact that the series will be a new adventure set in the wider franchise world. Nomura is working closely with the team behind the new series including the designs of its new characters as mentioned in his statement, and it’s going to be a joint production between Disney Kids & Family and Square Enix. Scheduled for a future release with Disney+, there’s unfortunately been no release window or date set for the new project as of this time.

Kingdom Hearts Is a Perfect Fit for Anime

Kingdom Hearts fans have been hoping for it to get an anime series pretty much as soon as it began. Thanks to its blend of Square Enix and Disney franchises it seemed a perfect fit for an animated take, but one has never really gotten off the ground. We’ve seen the franchise’s story expanded upon with official manga and light novel releases, but an anime would really be the final frontier. Now that Disney is open to anime projects like this and has found success with other franchises like Star Wars , it seems all the stars have properly aligned for it all at last.

Kingdom Hearts 4 is currently scheduled for a release in late 2027 , and that could be around the time we get to see this new anime series in action too. But it’s more likely that this series is scheduled for a release sometime in 2028 and beyond given that it seems very early into its production. But we’ll just have to see how much Disney and otherwise makes its way into this new anime.

title: One-Punch Man Season 3 Confirms Release Date for Next Major Update
content:
One-Punch Man made a very divisive return for Season 3 of the anime last year, and now it’s set to reveal a major update about the anime’s future later this Fall. One-Punch Man has had a very rough go at things when it comes to its anime adaptation over the last decade. As part of its celebration for its tenth anniversary milestone, the anime made a comeback for its third season. Unfortunately following a divisive response to the second season, the third season of episodes weren’t received any better than before .

One-Punch Man Season 3 wrapped up the first half of its run last year, and quickly confirmed that it would be returning for a second wave of episodes sometime in 2027. But while there have not been many updates as to the new season’s current progress as of this time, there’s going to be a major update shared for the few fans lucky to be in attendance at a panel coming during New York Comic Con 2026 this October.

One-Punch Man Season 3 Panel Announced for New York Comic Con 2026

One-Punch Man Season 3 will be hosting a special panel during the New York Comic Con 2026 weekend on Saturday, October 10th. It will feature Garou voice actor Hikaru Midorikawa making his first ever appearance at the convention, and is promising to have the next major update for what’s coming next in the season during the panel as well. While it’s yet to be revealed what kind of update could be coming for the new season, it’s the first notable update for these new episodes since they were first confirmed in 2025 .

This is part of why fans continue to worry about the state of One-Punch Man ‘s anime future thus far too. There was a lot of faith in the anime ahead of the third season’s debut as fans were really hoping that it would somehow bounce back from the second season. But with the same studio behind that divisive season coming back for the third, unfortunately it was not enough to save any of the faith fans had . Especially given that the third season had one rough episode after another.

What’s Going on With One-Punch Man Season 3?

One-Punch Man Season 3 Part 2 is currently scheduled for a release sometime in 2027, but has yet to confirm any concrete release date as of the time of this writing. There have been very few updates since the second half was announced to be in the works, but the anime has been breaking all sorts of records with fans despite this. There’s still a lot of faith from fans that the anime will bounce back from its poor reputation, but there are just as many signs that this won’t be the case.

One-Punch Man Season 3 is also in the midst of one of the anime’s longest arcs to date as the heroes face off against the Monster Association, and there’s quite a lot more to work through before this arc reaches its end. It’s possible that the anime might not even cover it all by the end of this third season, so make sure to catch up with it all now streaming with Hulu in the meantime just in case it does.

title: WEBTOON Acquires 60% Stake in Game Company RI Games Holdings to Expand Webtoons Into Games
content:
WEBTOON Entertainment announced on August 10 it has entered into a definitive agreement to make a strategic investment in RI Games Holdings Inc., a move that will give WEBTOON a 60% stake in the game company upon closing.

WEBTOON Entertainment plans to develop and release multiple games based on established webtoon IPs with global fanbases over the next four years. RI Games Holdings operates two game development studios, GrayGames and Offbeat.

RI Games Holdings' current lineup includes games based on popular webtoon titles Overgeared , which has accumulated 1.3 billion global views; Doom Breaker with 590 million views; and Omniscient Reader’s Viewpoint , which has surpassed 3.05 billion views.

The first title will be a new action MMORPG based on Overgeared . GrayGames is developing the game, with Nexon publishing it globally later this year. The game is scheduled to launch alongside the Overgeared anime, which will premiere in October.

The Overgeared anime revealed its first key visual, promotional video, and additional cast members in July. Crunchyroll also announced that it will stream the series. The anime is being produced by J.C. Staff , with Ayako Kōno directing.

Fans can read the official English versions of Doom Breaker and Omnisicent Reader's Viewpoint on WEBTOON and Overgeared on Tapas .

Omniscient Reader’s Viewpoint is also getting an upcoming anime adaptation. Offbeat's game adaptation, published by Com2uS, is slated for PC and console in 2028.

title: 6 Years Later, The Promised Neverland Returns for New Shonen Jump Sequel
content:
Ten years after it first began with Shueisha’s Weekly Shonen Jump magazine and six years after it ended, The Promised Neverland has made a surprise return with a brand new sequel entry. It’s big a milestone year for Shonen Jump as while there are a number of long running franchises coming to their respective ends, there are also many more that have begun celebrating huge milestones. That’s especially the case for The Promised Neverland , which is unfortunately had a rough go at things for the past few years thanks to its divisive anime adaptation .

Kaiu Shirai and Posuka Demizu’s The Promised Neverland has kicked off the tenth anniversary celebration of the manga’s original debut with Shueisha’s Weekly Shonen Jump magazine, and that celebration has kicked off with an official return of the series to the magazine itself. With the creators bringing the series back for a special new chapter set long after the events of the original series , this new sequel chapter helps to close one of the emotional loops left open years prior.

The Promised Neverland Returns for New Sequel for 10th Anniversary

The Promsied Neverland is celebrating its 10th anniversary with the release of a “special bonus chapter” titled “Undying Blade.” This is set in the year 2050, long after the end of the original series. Focusing on Ayshe, it finally resolves some of the lingering feelings that have been left behind by that original ending. Because while Emma was able to strike a new deal that would save humanity heading into the future, others like Ayshe still were left to carry the emotions of everything that happened to get to that grand finale point.

In the original series, Norman and the others had killed Ayshe’s father and that never really got resolved when all the fighting was done. This extra chapter reveals that she’s still struggling with the fact that she feels hatred over Norman and the others for killing her father despite the fact that she’s bonded with the other humans since. It’s something that she’s nearly violent over, but speaking with Emma she discovers that hope that she had been lacking this entire time.

What Does This Mean for The Promised Neverland’s Future?

This is only the first of many celebrations planned for The Promised Neverland’ s tenth anniversary, and fans will see more art and other smaller releases from the original creators behind it all to help commemorate its legacy. This is likely going to be the biggest of the projects, however, as it’s hard to top an official sequel story that picks up from the events of the original. But hopefully this sequel helps to salve some of the heat that has been brewing since the series came to its end. It’s still controversial to this day.

The Promised Neverland didn’t have a traditional end to its main conflict as revealed through this sequel chapter as Emma lost her memories of everything that happened as the result of a final deal. And things got even more divisive when the anime adaptation decided to butcher nearly 65% of the manga’s story in favor of speeding to its own grand finale in just two single seasons. But then again, we still talk about after all these years so that has to mean something.

title: Hanashi Media Licenses The Hated Prince's Do-Over, The Sage of the Forbidden Library, 6 More Light Novels
content:
English and Spanish book publisher Hanashi Media announced in July and August it has licensed the following light novels for release in English:

After years of crushing taxes and rampant corruption among the nobility, the people rise up in revolution—and Arthur Pendragon, the second prince of Britain, is sent straight to the guillotine.

But when Arthur opens his eyes, he finds himself five years in the past!

Desperate to avoid the execution awaiting him, Arthur racks his brain for a way to change his fate. Then, after casually showing a little kindness to a maid, a mysterious voice echoes inside his head:

“Good Deed Points have been awarded. The future has shifted slightly.”

Realizing this mysterious voice may be his only hope for survival, Arthur resolves to start treating everyone kindly. Not because he has suddenly become a better person, of course—but because he desperately wants to stay alive!

And so begins the do-over of a cowardly, petty, slightly overconfident, and utterly hopeless prince. To save his own neck, he'll do everything he can to win over the people—and even the entire world!

Cero, a priest of light, shields the Hero from the Sixth Demon Lord's curse—only to be transformed into a demon himself. As his reward, he is cast out of the Hero's party and forcibly teleported far away.

At his destination, Cero encounters Lucy, the Sixth Demon Lord's daughter, who recognizes in him the potential to become a Demon Lord. Together with the demons now serving under him, Cero sets out to develop his new territory.

Then, one day, the Hero's party arrives to eliminate him. But when they venture into the tomato field outside Cero's castle, they discover monsters lurking among the crops—each one enhanced by Cero's abilities!

What was supposed to be a simple field of tomatoes may prove to be the most unconquerable dungeon of all!

“You're the only one who's special to me.”

When Koutaro Nakayama returns to school after classes to retrieve something he forgot, he finds Shiho Shimotsuki fast asleep in an empty classroom.

Rumor has it that Shiho is the girl Ryoma Ryuzaki truly has his sights set on. Popular with seemingly every girl in class, Ryoma is already well on his way to forming a harem. Yet Shiho remains as expressionless as ever—not a single person has ever seen her smile.

So why are her pale fingers wrapped around Koutaro's hand?!

And so begins a secret relationship between the heroine and the background character she was never supposed to notice!

Thanks to her extraordinary talent and remarkable achievements, Elysia is the only apprentice librarian permitted to enter the Forbidden Library alone, where countless mysterious and dangerous magical tomes are kept. She believes this will allow her to continue her magical research in peace.

But on the day she turns fifteen and officially comes of age, a divine oracle unexpectedly declares her a Sage.

The birth of the first Sage in centuries throws the entire kingdom into an uproar, but Elysia couldn't be less thrilled. With the Royal Ministry of Magic firmly on her side, she retreats into the unexplored depths of the Forbidden Library—only to discover a girl frozen in ice!

An unparalleled talent is about to rewrite history. A grand fantasy of magical discovery starring a brilliant young prodigy begins!

Its name? “Breeding Man”!

Getting women in the mood and guaranteeing pregnancy after sleeping with them is only the beginning. He's an exceptional rider—and no, not in that sense. He can expertly wield spears—the weapons—and rods—the fishing kind—and can even tame wild animals—literally—and turn them into livestock!

Through increasingly ridiculous interpretations of his ability, Matabei begins rising through the ranks as a samurai and developing his own territory.

An unprecedented tale of reincarnation, conquest, and unrivaled “spear work” in the Sengoku era begins!

And countless challengers will fall before him in his battles after dark: a shrine maiden, a samurai's daughter, an Iga kunoichi, and even Nobunaga of the Oda clan…

Wait, what?!

“This isn't what you promised! This isn't what you promised! This isn't what you promised at all!”

The voice belongs to Lina, an eight-year-old girl who enlisted in the military to save the orphanage that raised her. She can't wield a sword or use magic. All she has is the unassuming skill Multilingual Comprehension—and memories of a past life spent enduring endless overtime at an exploitative company and playing strategy simulation games!

Lina was promised a well-paid desk job at a safe command post. Instead, she finds herself in the middle of the battlefield, forced into the role of a mysterious military strategist.

No one yet realizes that the commands issued by her tiny hands will overturn every convention and completely transform the course of the war—not even Lina herself.

As for Lina, she has only one desperate request: a slice of deliciously sweet cake.

After being reincarnated from a hard-charging career in the trading business, Sara finds herself plotting her future from within the marquis's household that has taken her in. If she remains an unwelcome guest, the best she can hope for is becoming some nobleman's second wife, forever looked down upon for her commoner origins.

Her solution? Take full advantage of the backing of her wealthy new family while making a strategic retreat to their remote territory, where she can quietly build up enough capital to strike out on her own.

At least, that was the plan…

When Sara arrives, she discovers that embezzlement has pushed the territory to the brink of financial ruin! With her all-important patron in trouble, there's no point in playing the sweet, innocent little girl anymore.

Using long-forgotten alchemical research buried in the castle as leverage, Sara begins headhunting talented personnel. She pressures the guild into developing the local mines to secure a new source of income, all while throwing the adults around her completely off balance as she works to rebuild the territory's economy.

And before long, at only eight years old, Sara is already setting out on the path to building a mercantile empire powerful enough to have even a marquis at her beck and call!

Family, adults, nobles—it doesn't matter who stands in her way. Armed with a sharp business mind and an eye for profit, this merchant heiress is ready to make a fortune!

“Traveling sounds nice, for example.”

As if the universe heard him, his journey begins sooner than expected. On his way home, he suddenly finds himself stranded in another world—a strange, game-like place governed by levels, magic, skills, and other fantastical rules. And before he knows it, he's acquired tremendous power without even having to work for it.

With that kind of strength at his disposal, three paths lie before him: side with humanity and become a hero, join the demons and unleash chaos upon the world… or choose neither and use his newfound power for nothing more than his own amusement.

For him, the choice is obvious.

And so begins one thirty-something nobody's journey through another world, living exactly as he pleases until he gets bored!
author: ANN

title: 5 Beloved Shonen Series With Disappointing Endings
content:
Shonen is the most popular demographic in the anime and manga industry, known for its variety of stories across fantasy and other genres. For several decades, most successful anime and manga franchises have been from the same demographic. However, just as Shonen is loved for its unique stories, many such series are also equally criticized for disappointing endings. Even some of the classic series often end up disappointing fans with their anticlimactic endings. Whether it’s the unexpected twist during the end of the serialization or the creator facing burnout due to a weekly schedule, the reasons behind such disappointing endings vary.

Regardless, while the anime can somewhat save the ending with original scenes or better adaptation, the overall conclusion can never be changed. The five beloved Shonen listed below are some of the most legendary series of all time, yet their endings are far from satisfying.

5) Attack on Titan

Attack on Titan finally managed to save its ending thanks to MAPPA’s exceptional adaptation. However, during the time of the serialization, the final stretch of the manga was heavily criticized for the direction the story took due to the Rumbling. Whether it’s the insane plot twist at the end or Eren’s death, the ending was hated for many reasons. Even if the anime did manage to soothe fans with the adaptation, the series still took the direction that was originally intended.

Not to mention that Hajime Isayama faced a lot of stress during the time, and he still hasn’t returned with a new series even more than five years since the manga’s conclusion. Attack on Titan is one of the highest-rated series of all time, and fans love it now more than ever. However, the controversy from back then was still immense, and it’s a miracle that the series managed to save itself from what could’ve been the biggest blunder in Shonen history.

4) Naruto

Not many fans would want to admit it, but Naruto ‘s ending still leaves a bitter feeling after the appearance of Kagaya Otsutsuki. The series instilled fear among everyone by hyping Madara Uchiha as the final antagonist, and things were going fine until Black Zetsu revealed that the legendary Shinobi was nothing more than a puppet. Madara’s actions were guided by Zetsu in order to free Kagaya from the eternal prison. Even now, the ending often receives mixed reactions, especially in the manga that doesn’t feature an entire arc after the final war.

The anime followed the characters after the final war in filler episodes, giving them individual conclusions, which was way better than how the manga handled things. The manga wrapped right after the battle between Naruto and Sasuke, with an extra chapter released later on to hype up the sequel spin-off, Boruto. This is also the reason why the anime is more loved worldwide compared to the manga despite having so many filler episodes. Although the series is considered a classic, Kagaya’s appearance will always be met with criticism due to the last-minute plot twist.

3) Bleach

Another classic series on our list is Bleach, another one of the Shonen Big Three. Bleach ended a decade ago, and the series never really saved its reputation from the controversial ending until the anime confirmed adapting the final arc. Whether it’s the unanswered questions or the open-ended and rushed finale with a sudden timeskip, the ending was criticized for several years. It also worsened the series’ reputation within the Shonen Big Three despite having an exceptional story and world-building. During that time, Tite Kubo was struggling with health issues, which severely impacted his work.

Luckily, the anime adaptation in the Thousand-Year Blood War is more than enough to make up for it. Released in four cours, the final arc in the anime not only has exceptional animation and pacing, but the original scenes add more depth to the overall story. It’s also been confirmed that the finale will be a bit different from the manga . Kubo has been actively involved with the anime adaptation in the final arc, providing original character designs and scripts to ensure a better conclusion.

2) Jujutsu Kaisen

Jujutsu Kaisen ‘s ending is somewhat less hated now due to the epilogue in the final volume and the sequel manga . However, it still wasn’t enough to save the disappointing manga finale, which barely left any room to follow the aftermath. The Shinjuku Showdown Arc was simply just one battle after another, without giving the story any space to breathe for development. After the fast-paced action, the series ended without ever explaining Yuji’s Domain Expansion.

There were several unanswered questions during the ending that were never explained, which isn’t what you’d expect from a series that popular. Leaving things unanswered during the finale is the major reason why Jujutsu Kaisen will always be remembered as having one of the worst endings of all time. Despite the disappointment, the series’ popularity has only continued to increase with a successful anime adaptation and over 150 million copies of manga in circulation.

1) Demon Slayer

It’s been more than six years since the manga reached its conclusion, and to be honest, not even the anime can save it. The Infinity Castle Arc was still impressive with the matchups and the backstories, along with so many intense battles. However, things took a completely different turn during the Sunrise Countdown Arc when the surviving Corps members faced off against Muzan Kibutsuji. It’s difficult to appreciate an ending when more than half of the cast has been killed off during the brutal battle. Not to mention that the plot twist after Muzan’s defeat only prolongs the suffering of Tanjiro and others when the demon tried to take control of him.

While the final chapter gave a sense of bittersweet ending, it’s also important to remember that it wasn’t the beloved characters who got their happy endings, but they were either the descendants or their reincarnations with no memories of the past. The night-long battle continued for the entire Infinity Castle and the Sunrise Countdown Arc, with barely one chapter to follow the aftermath. Even years after the ending, the manga never returned with an extra release or a spin-off to carry on its legacy. Despite that, Demon Slayer is one of the most successful anime and manga series of all time, and its popularity only continues to increase thanks to the trilogy.
